sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Global Ocean is a BSE SME freight-forwarding coordinator, not a shipowner. The strongest evidence is growing shipment activity and FY26 operating profitability; the decisive weakness is profit that has not converted into cash, alongside unresolved connected-advance and disclosure reconciliations. At the stale last-observed ₹107.77 on 16 October, the business is an unresolved cash-conversion/special-situation research candidate, not an evidence-backed compounder or an eligible investment setup. BQS, Growth Quality GQS and IAS are all NS, not low numeric ranks. G2/G3 are Hold. A conditional unchanged-March-cash base model yields 9.45% over five investor years, below the 15% hurdle, but this is not an ordinary investor return or actionable entry price. Current funding proof, clean reconciliations and sustained collections would change the evidence status; a lower quote alone would not resolve governance or cash questions.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company arranges ocean and air freight, container-freight-station services, inland road/rail movements, customs clearance, project cargo and third-party logistics through carriers and service partners. It does not disclose owned ships or immovable property. FY26 revenue ₹207.859 cr includes ocean ₹127.288 cr (61.24%), CFS ₹59.4991 cr (28.62%) and air ₹5.1209 cr (2.46%); other services complete the mix. Revenue is collected from shippers while carriers/CFS suppliers are paid separately; the economically important spread is much smaller than freight billed. Prospectus accounting excludes reimbursable expenses from revenue while some customers deduct tax on gross invoices, making reported invoices, economic throughput and retained income distinct. Foreign-shipment income ₹2.3823 cr is in other income but retained in the economic EBITDA proxy; all nonoperating interest/rent/refund income ₹0.7787 cr is excluded. Contracts, carrier space, staff and relationships matter more than factory utilization. Fixed-capital intensity is low, but receivables/prepaids and unsecured loans mean total capital demand is not low. Geographic/customer mix and annual FY26 shipment volumes require an update; no invented capacity utilization or market share is supplied.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text:
A repeat-customer network can reduce coordination errors and support service quality, but evidence of durable pricing power, proprietary technology or a cost advantage is insufficient. FY25 largest customer 18.58%, top 10 42.21%; H1FY26 top 10 increases to 48.55%. Customer names are withheld for consent, a disclosure gap rather than evidence of related dealing. FY25 largest supplier 7.42%, top 10 43.43%, across 395 suppliers; access is diversified but carriers still influence freight economics.182 customers with relationships longer than three years generated ₹125.4155 cr FY25, supporting retention without proving switching barriers.

Three economically relevant peers in the dated IPO comparison are Blue Water, Tiger Logistics and S J Logistics.

| FY25 issuer-compiled comparator | Revenue cr | EBITDA margin | PAT cr | Debt/equity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Global Ocean | 190.5591 | 4.93% | 6.8151 | .07 |
| Blue Water | 196.1804 | 9.56% | 10.6708 | 1.82 |
| Tiger | 536.3050 | 5.76% | 27.0247 | .25 |
| S J | 502.4895 | 15.00% | 52.4936 | .28 |

Blue Water is weaker on leverage in this snapshot, but better on margin; Tiger/SJ have larger scale and different project/NVOCC exposure. Thus no single peer is a clean superior or inferior business across dimensions. Figures are issuer-compiled, not independently reconciled current peer accounts; matched 19 October peer multiples are ND. The model uses an explicit 7–13 x terminal EV/EBITDA sensitivity rather than pretending it is a verified sector median.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text:
Comparable reported revenue was ₹189.0095 cr FY23,₹102.2024 cr FY24,₹190.5591 cr FY25 and ₹207.859 cr FY26: the selected three-year CAGR is 3.2195%. FY24 fell 45.93%, FY25 rebounded 86.45%, FY26 grew 9.08%; this volatility cautions against a straight growth narrative. The first full FY22₹73.3282 cr to FY26 four-year CAGR 29.7551% is disclosed as context, not substituted to obtain a better score. FY21₹0.5989 cr covers only 8 January–31 March, so mechanical five-year 222.17% is invalid as comparable organic growth and the comparable five-year metric is null. Annual additions are ₹72.7293,115.6813,−86.8071,88.3567,17.2999 cr from FY21 onward.

TEUs 22,361/21,597/29,094 and shipments 7,110/7,288/10,384 in FY23/24/25 imply two-year CAGRs 14.066%/20.850%. H1FY26 TEUs 18,916 and 5,738 shipments are not annualized into invented full-year numbers. Revenue less service cost plus foreign-shipment income grows 21.6524% CAGR over FY23–26, a useful retained-spread proxy but not audited net revenue. Price, mix, principal-agent differences and acquisitions are not sufficiently decomposed; no acquisition-driven growth was identified, but this does not prove a fully organic bridge. REV is NS because the economic-growth series required for this business is incomplete, not because the mathematically correct gross-sales CAGR is unknown.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Demand for trade logistics is enduring, but the accessible runway must be won shipment by shipment, at a retained spread, and financed through collections. Doubling shipments does not double intrinsic value if credit terms expand or service spreads compress. The proposed Hong Kong subsidiary may broaden counterparties; the ₹-equivalent cash requirement, actual capitalization and operating profitability are not verified. No management promise of automatic profitable global expansion is adopted.

March operating working capital is ₹26.1108 cr: receivables 32.5596 + prepaids 6.1992 + government balances 1.0352 + forward receivable 0.1846 + staff advances 0.5349 − payables 13.8565 − other operating liabilities 0.5462. Add operating PPE 0.6923 and security deposits 0.473 for asset-approach operating capital 27.2761 cr. Nonstaff loan assets 9.726 cr are separated, not mistaken for customer-serving operating investment. No matching cohort-level incremental NOPAT/capital/time series exists; reported ROCE 39.5% cannot repair CAP NS. Base growth 10% needs receivables 60 days, payables 27 days, prepaids 3% and capex 0.4% of sales. These are explicit assumptions, not contracted funding terms. CASH 2 caps a complete GQS at 5; with REV/CAP missing, final GQS remains NS. Growth quality will improve only when repeated activity produces cash and attributable incremental returns, not merely when EPS grows.

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
sections.text:
Promoters' industry experience predates the 2021 corporate entity; it must not be confused with five comparable public-company years. December 2025 promoter ownership 59.86% and no reported encumbrance are dated facts; current September primary shareholding/pledge evidence is missing. Director remuneration ₹0.90 cr, including MD ₹0.60 cr, is material but not by itself excessive or abusive. Related services, rent and loans need commercial and collection scrutiny; management says they are approved, ordinary-course and arms-length.

The audit page uses “Opinion” and “Basis for Opinion” and says “gives a true and fair view”; the directors page 27 says “with a qualified opinion” and also “does not contain any qualification, reservation, adverse remark or disclaimer”. These short exact excerpts preserve the contradiction. The displayed auditor opinion is unmodified on financial results; do not allege a formal qualification or certify a full statutory/CARO scope not located.

IPO 3,899,200 shares at ₹78 raised ₹30.41376 cr. Annual accounts deduct ₹5.7078 cr issuance expense; May utilization certificate uses ₹4.5832 cr, leaving ₹1.1246 cr unexplained. It claims working capital ₹21.2685 cr, GCP ₹4.5621 cr, expenses ₹4.5832 cr and zero unused proceeds. Its dates imply IPO December 2026 and use through September 2025, inconsistent with the actual December 2025 IPO. Results note also uses ₹66 premium versus verified ₹68 and a 2026 closing date. These appear transcription/clerical inconsistencies requiring correction, not proof of diversion.

| Commitment / event | Dated observation | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IPO/listing | Listed 24 December 2025; current shares match master | Delivered financing, not operating return |
| IPO deployment | May 30 claims fully utilized; account expense differs | Unreconciled; obtain bank/object ledger |
| CSR | FY26 required 0.1188 cr, spent 0;0.125 cr transferred 16 June | Transfer not final project spending; ongoing-project wording conflicts |
| HK expansion | June 25 approval, up to HK$1 m,3–4 week expectation | Incorporation/remittance/result not verified |
| BSE price query | May 27 management says market-driven, no knowledge/control | Response preserved; inquiry not misconduct finding |

RPT note totals ₹4.1313 cr while note 16 subcategory is ₹2.1222 cr. The RPT note is not an additional asset; its mapping across note 16 staff/nonstaff buckets remains unresolved. The model retains one 9.726 cr nonstaff pool as a conservative assumption, without asserting an exact RPT subset. G1 remains Conditional, G2 Hold; strong allegations would exceed the evidence.

sections.text:
At ₹107.77 and 1.4442691 crore shares, marketcap ₹155.6489 cr. Current-claim reportedP/E15.2034 x, P/B 2.9759 x; using reportedweighted EPS would misleadingly show 12.2050 x. Datedgross-cash EV ₹140.5766 cr and EV/economic EBITDA 10.6259 x are not verified current EV. Retaining operating cash floor and CSR gives EV ₹144.8588 cr. Normalized PAT ₹9.5480 cr at 26% tax is a proxy, not an audited adjustment.

All ordinary investor IRRs and ordinary hurdle entries are null. The table below contains only assumed-anchor diagnostics: five complete investor years 19 October 2026–19 October 2031, Marchbalances assumed unchanged atOctober, no FY32 interpolation or post-terminal financing. Annualtax, workingcapital, capex, debt, loan recoveries, cash floor and dilution are fully embedded. No dividends;1% entry/2% exit friction, pre-investor-tax.

Base conditional 15% hurdle entry ₹84.16 is not an ordinary actionable entry because current funding is unverified. DCF uses the same FCFF less cash-floor reinvestment, maturegrowth 2–4%, discount 12–18% (not assertedWACC), openingcash abovefloor only, discounted loan recoveries once, and no futurecash pile doublecount. At 15%/3%, diagnosticprice ₹61.87 and terminalshare EV 69.33%. It differs from the 10 x multiple model because the terminal capitalization assumption is more conservative, not because cash is counted twice. Reverseexpectations require 17.3785% revenueCAGR to 463.139 cr at 6% margin/10 x to reach 15% after friction, with base collections and 50% loanrecovery. Forecasts are sensitivities, not guidance. Growth 5/10/15% ×multiple 8/10/12, margin−2 pp, DSO+30, payables 15 days, no legacyrecoveries, adverse tax, unavailable FD, and execution-cost grids are included below and in machine-readable model.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is a linked operating and funding shock: loss or repricing of a major customer reduces revenue 20%; carriers demand faster payment while collections extend to 100 days; retained EBITDAmargin falls to 2.5%; prepaids rise to 5% of sales; related/other loans do not return; an additional ₹1 cr leaves in each of the firsttwo years; legacy tax ₹1.5813 cr and a 10% receivable loss ₹3.25596 cr consume cash once. No magical bank drawdown or automatic equity rescue is allowed. Minimum net new cash needed to preserve 2% revenue operatingfloor is ₹11.9336 cr under annual arithmetic; intrayear stress could be worse. The unfinanced terminal equity formula is not a real realizable distribution and no conditionalIRR is displayed for it.

A separately labeled equity rescue demonstrates price and fee dilution, not feasibility: even funding the gap leaves a large loss to today's holder. Low debt and IPO cash are meaningful counterarguments, and the model is not a forecast of insolvency. The key falsification variable is sustained conversion of freight earnings into unrestricted cash after fair-value connected advances and normal workingcapital. If collections and commercial advance terms cannot be substantiated, lowP/E or bookvalue cannot establish a margin of safety. Conversely, verified current FD availability, bank-confirmed collections and corrected reconciliations would weaken this bear thesis substantially. No probability is assigned without evidence.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A five-year 5× price outcome requires 37.973% annual price appreciation;10× requires 58.489%. Ignoring dilution and netclaim changes merely for an algebraic firstcheck, today’s ₹155.6489 cr equity value becomes ₹778.2444/₹1,556.4888 cr. At 10 x EV/EBITDA and 6% margin that implies revenue about ₹1,297.07/₹2,594.15 cr, multiples of current ₹207.859 cr. This is not a funded forecast: growing such gross freight revenue needs workingcapital, customer wins, retainedspreads and control of connected cashoutflows. Any dilutive rescue raises the business growth required for the same per-share return; a lower terminal multiple raises it further. No verified marketshare gain, cohortreturn or cash-funded runway supports those endpoints. Both 5× and 10× are Speculative / unsupported overfive years. Small marketcap alone is not optionality worth paying for; the defensible question is whether cash earnings per current diluted share can compound after necessary capital, not whether freight invoices can expand.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: Hold — unresolved financial reliability/current funding; insufficient evidence for numeric BQS/GQS/IAS ranking. Research priority is evidence resolution, not eligible-for-investment consideration. It fails the evidence-backed compounder criteria because several canonical inputs are NS, CASH is 2 and critical gates remain unresolved, not because the SME label itself is disqualifying. There is no requested holding data, weight, tax basis or risk budget, so no portfolio exit count or trade instruction is inferred.

The stale quote and lot granularity matter: one 1,600-sharelot costs ₹172,432; ₹5 lakh rounds down to 3,200 shares / ₹344,864 or up to 4,800 shares / ₹517,296 before costs. Only 15/20 and 40/60 sessions are observed. The 60-session observed close×volume median ₹849,880 andmean ₹2,035,446 are proxies, not actualturnover. Unknown nonnegative days imply a mathematical median-capacity range ₹343,920–₹1,760,000, not zero-trade imputations. At 5% participation,₹5 lakh continuous arithmetic spans 5.68–29.08 days; actual lots are stricter: known 60-day 5% capacity totals 12 lots on only 4 observedeligible days, giving 10/15 equivalentdays for 2/3 lots, not a forecast of executable exits. Current bid/ask, circuit limits, restrictions and pledge remain unverified. L stays NS.

A lower price could improve conditional valuation but cannot cure data gates. Reopening requires bank-confirmed unrestricted cash and obligations, corrected audited/proceeds/RPT reconciliations, collections evidence, full current shareholding and official liquidity. Only then can an ordinary funding-consistent return and entry threshold be scored.

The source register below links each material claim to a dated primary document or clearly labeled secondary observation. V=verified transcription, M=management/accountant claim, C=calculation, A=analyst assumption. Verified transcription is not independent certification of a company's economic truth. Original PDFs, extracted raw text and page images remain local only; private backups contain selected safe financial tables, research, code, results and sourceURLs/hashes, not issuer PDFs/OCR/personal identifiers. Reproduction reruns calculations from frozen inputs and is separate from primary-source verification.

Missing answers stay missing; no external outreach or recurring monitor is authorized.

All forecasts are in ₹crore exceptper-share rupees, reflect 15% nominal pre-tax hurdle, and are annualinvestor-year arithmetic rather than an interim liquidity certificate. Cashfloor 2% ofrevenue is an explicit analyst assumption. No forecast return is represented as reliable while current funding is unverified. summary: Global Ocean is a BSE SME freight-forwarding coordinator, not a shipowner. The strongest evidence is growing shipment activity and FY26 operating profitability; the decisive weakness is profit that has not converted into cash, alongside unresolved connected-advance and disclosure reconciliations. At the stale last-observed ₹107.77 on 16 October, the business is an unresolved cash-conversion/special-situation research candidate, not an evidence-backed compounder or an eligible investment setup. BQS, Growth Quality GQS and IAS are all NS, not low numeric ranks. G2/G3 are Hold. A conditional unchanged-March-cash base model yields 9.45% over five investor years, below the 15% hurdle, but this is not an ordinary investor return or actionable entry price. Current funding proof, clean reconciliations and sustained collections would change the evidence status; a lower quote alone would not resolve governance or cash questions.
